title: Java Comments
learningObjectives: Write a single-line Java comment using //.
Write a multi-line Java comment using /* and */.
Recognize documentation comments that begin with /**.
Explain that comments are ignored by the Java compiler as program instructions.
Use comments to clarify intent without duplicating obvious code.

understand.concept: Comments are notes written in source code for people who read or maintain it. Java supports single-line comments beginning with `//`, multi-line comments enclosed by `/*` and `*/`, and documentation comments beginning with `/**` and ending with `*/`. Comments are not executed as program statements.
understand.whyItMatters: Useful comments explain intent, constraints or non-obvious decisions. They help another developer understand why code exists, but comments that merely repeat the code can become misleading when the code changes.
understand.analogy: A comment is like a margin note in a textbook: it gives the reader extra context without changing the printed instructions.
understand.analogyLimit: A comment does not make incorrect code correct, and it is not a substitute for clear names, tests or documentation. Documentation comments can be processed by tools such as javadoc.

explain.narrative:
## Single-line comments

Start a single-line comment with `//`. The comment continues to the end of that source line.

## Multi-line comments

Use `/*` to begin and `*/` to end a block comment. It can span multiple lines. Avoid placing another block comment inside one.

## Documentation comments

A documentation comment begins with `/**` and is commonly placed before a class, method or field. Tools such as `javadoc` can read these comments and generate API documentation.

## Comment quality

Explain why a non-obvious decision was made, document assumptions or warn about a constraint. Update or remove comments when the implementation changes.

examples.title: Single-line comment
examples.explanation: The compiler treats text after // on that line as a comment, not an executable statement.

examples.title: Block and documentation comments
examples.explanation: The documentation comment describes the class, while the block comment explains the sample value. Neither changes output.

practise.guidedTask: Add one // comment above a println statement explaining its purpose. Add one short block comment above a sample variable.
practise.independentTask: Write a short method and add a documentation comment above it stating what it does and what its parameter means. Keep the comment accurate if the method changes.
hints: Use // for a comment that ends with the line.
Use /** ... */ before API elements when documentation tools should process the description.
practise.challenge: Review your program against the expected behaviour, then explain one likely error and how you would diagnose it.

questions.prompt: Which token begins a Java single-line comment?
questions.explanation: A double slash begins a single-line comment.

questions.prompt: Which delimiters enclose a traditional block comment?
questions.explanation: A block comment begins with /* and ends with */.

questions.prompt: What is a documentation comment commonly used for?
options: Describing API elements for tools such as javadoc
questions.answer: Describing API elements for tools such as javadoc
questions.explanation: Documentation comments can be processed to generate API documentation.

questions.prompt: Do Java comments execute as program statements?
questions.explanation: Comments are ignored as executable instructions by the compiler.

questions.prompt: Which comment is most useful when explaining a non-obvious design decision?
options: A concise comment that explains why the decision was made
A comment that repeats every character of the next line
A comment that is never updated
questions.answer: A concise comment that explains why the decision was made
questions.explanation: Good comments add context that is not already obvious from the code.
